title: Association between prenatal glucocorticoid exposure and adolescent neurodevelopment: An observational follow-up study.
ehr_evidence: Pregnancy and birth data were obtained from hospital records or the German maternity passport.
summary: Prospective observational follow-up study assessing the long-term effects of prenatal betamethasone exposure on cognitive performance, neuroendocrine stress reactivity, autonomic nervous system activity, and electrocortical activity in 14- to 15-year-old adolescents.
key_findings: No statistically significant difference in global IQ between betamethasone-exposed and unexposed groups (adjusted mean difference −2.0, 95% CI: −7.12 to 3.12, p = 0.44).
No significant differences in ADHD symptoms, BMI, or HOMA-IR between groups.
No significant differences in HPAA or ANS activity overall.

Betamethasone-exposed adolescents exhibited reduced electrocortical activity in the frontal brain region compared to controls (adjusted SEF 16.0 Hz vs 17.8 Hz, mean difference −1.83 Hz, 95% CI: −3.21 to −0.45, p = 0.01).
data_source_type: Direct clinical assessments, questionnaires, biological sampling, and historical hospital/maternity records
population: 56 adolescents aged 14–15 years (21 exposed to prenatal betamethasone, 35 unexposed controls), born at term or near-term in Germany
limitations: Small sample size and reduced statistical power
Selective participation and loss to follow-up
Possible confounding by tocolytic treatment and late preterm birth
